concepts.title: Types of Farming
concepts.definition: Farming in India is broadly classified into primitive subsistence farming, intensive subsistence farming, and commercial farming based on the purpose, scale, and level of technology used.
concepts.key_idea: Subsistence farming is practised to meet the needs of the farmer's family; commercial farming uses modern inputs and grows crops for the market.
question_patterns: Differentiate between subsistence and commercial farming.
What is primitive subsistence farming and where is it practised?
Explain intensive subsistence farming with examples.
How does commercial farming differ from subsistence farming in inputs?
Why is shifting agriculture called primitive subsistence farming?

solution_steps.explain: Classify the described practice as primitive subsistence, intensive subsistence, or commercial farming.
Check whether the produce is for self-consumption or market and note the level of modern inputs used.
Conclude the farming type based on purpose, scale, and technology.

worked_examples.question: A farmer in Assam grows rice on a small plot using family labour and consumes most of the produce. What type of farming is this?
worked_examples.solution: The produce is mainly for self-consumption on a small holding with high labour input, which is intensive subsistence farming.

worked_examples.question: A large farm in Punjab uses tractors, HYV seeds, and chemical fertilisers to grow wheat for sale. Identify the farming type.
worked_examples.solution: Modern inputs are used and the output is sold in the market, which is commercial farming.

exercises.question: Distinguish between primitive and intensive subsistence farming.
Give one example each of subsistence and commercial farming practised in India.
Explain how the purpose of production distinguishes subsistence from commercial farming.

concepts.title: Cropping Patterns
concepts.definition: Cropping pattern refers to the proportion of area under different crops at a point of time. Major patterns include rabi, kharif, and zaid crops grown across different seasons.
concepts.key_idea: Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in spring; kharif crops are sown with the monsoon and harvested in autumn; zaid crops are grown in the short summer season.
question_patterns: What are the three major cropping seasons in India?
Name two rabi and two kharif crops.
When are zaid crops grown and give examples.
How does the monsoon influence the kharif cropping pattern?
Differentiate between rabi and kharif cropping seasons.

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the crop is rabi, kharif, or zaid from the sowing and harvest months.
List typical crops associated with the identified season such as wheat for rabi and rice for kharif.
Relate the season to rainfall and temperature requirements.

worked_examples.question: Wheat is sown in October-November and harvested in March-April. Which cropping season does it belong to?
worked_examples.solution: Crops sown in winter and harvested in spring belong to the rabi season.

worked_examples.question: Paddy is sown in June-July with the onset of the monsoon and harvested in September-October. Identify the cropping season.
worked_examples.solution: Crops sown with the monsoon and harvested in autumn are kharif crops.

exercises.question: List two rabi and two kharif crops with their sowing seasons.
What are zaid crops? Give two examples.
Explain how rainfall distribution determines the kharif cropping pattern in India.

concepts.title: Major Crop: Rice
concepts.definition: Rice is the staple food crop of a majority of the people of India. It requires high temperature (above 25 degrees C), high humidity, and annual rainfall above 100 cm.
concepts.key_idea: Rice is a kharif crop grown in the plains of north and north-eastern India, coastal areas, and deltaic regions; it is also grown in areas of less rainfall with irrigation.
question_patterns: What climatic conditions are required for rice cultivation?
Name the major rice-producing states of India.
Why is rice grown in deltaic regions?
How is rice cultivation possible in regions of low rainfall?
Explain the geographical distribution of rice in India.

solution_steps.explain: Note the temperature, rainfall, and humidity needed for rice.
List the major states and deltaic/plains regions where rice is grown.
Describe how irrigation supports rice in low-rainfall areas.

worked_examples.question: Which temperature and rainfall are ideal for rice?
worked_examples.solution: Rice needs above 25 degrees C temperature, high humidity, and above 100 cm annual rainfall.
worked_examples.answer: Above 25 degrees C and above 100 cm rainfall

worked_examples.question: Name two leading rice-producing states in India.
worked_examples.solution: West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh are among the leading rice producers.

exercises.question: Describe the climatic conditions required for rice cultivation.
Why is rice cultivation possible in Punjab despite low rainfall?
Explain the distribution of rice production in India with examples.

concepts.title: Major Crop: Wheat
concepts.definition: Wheat is the second most important cereal crop and the main food crop in north and north-western India. It requires a cool growing season and bright sunshine at the time of ripening.
concepts.key_idea: Wheat is a rabi crop needing 10-15 degrees C at sowing, 21-26 degrees C at harvest, and about 75 cm annual rainfall; major producers are Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, and Haryana.
question_patterns: What are the climatic requirements of wheat?
Name the major wheat-producing states of India.
Why is wheat grown as a rabi crop?
Compare the rainfall requirements of rice and wheat.
Explain the distribution of wheat in India.

solution_steps.explain: Note the cool growing season and bright sunshine at ripening.
List the major wheat-producing states in the north and north-west.
Contrast wheat's lower rainfall need with rice's higher requirement.

worked_examples.question: What temperature range suits wheat cultivation?
worked_examples.solution: Wheat needs 10-15 degrees C at sowing and 21-26 degrees C at harvest.

worked_examples.question: Name two leading wheat-producing states.
worked_examples.solution: Uttar Pradesh and Punjab are leading wheat producers.

exercises.question: Describe the climatic conditions required for wheat.
Why is wheat mainly grown in northern India?
Compare the geographical and climatic requirements of rice and wheat.

concepts.title: Millets and Pulses
concepts.definition: Millets (jowar, bajra, ragi) are coarse grains grown in dry regions with low rainfall. Pulses (tur, arhar, gram, urad) are leguminous crops that enrich soil fertility by fixing nitrogen.
concepts.key_idea: Millets are hardy crops suited to arid conditions; pulses are the major source of protein in the Indian diet and restore soil nitrogen.
question_patterns: Why are millets called coarse grains and where are they grown?
How do pulses help in maintaining soil fertility?
Name three important millets grown in India.
Which is the leading pulse-producing state in India?
Explain the nutritional importance of pulses.

solution_steps.explain: Classify the crop as a millet or a pulse from its description.
Note the rainfall and soil needs -- millets in dry regions, pulses in light soils.
Describe the nutritional or soil-fertility benefit of the crop group.

worked_examples.question: Ragi is grown in Karnataka. Which crop group does it belong to and why?
worked_examples.solution: Ragi is a millet, a coarse grain suited to dry regions.

worked_examples.question: How do pulses improve soil fertility?
worked_examples.solution: Pulses are leguminous and fix atmospheric nitrogen in the soil, restoring fertility.
worked_examples.answer: By fixing nitrogen in the soil

exercises.question: Name three millets and one leading producing state for each.
Explain why pulses are called leguminous crops.
Discuss the importance of millets and pulses in Indian agriculture.

concepts.title: Food Crops vs Cash Crops
concepts.definition: Food crops (rice, wheat, millets, pulses) are grown to provide food grains; cash crops (cotton, jute, sugarcane, oilseeds, tea, coffee) are grown primarily for sale and industrial use.
concepts.key_idea: Food crops meet dietary needs while cash crops generate income and supply raw material to industries.
question_patterns: Differentiate between food crops and cash crops with examples.
Why are sugarcane and cotton called cash crops?
Name two cash crops and the industry linked to each.
How do cash crops contribute to the economy?
Give one example each of a food crop and a cash crop grown in India.

solution_steps.explain: Decide whether the crop is a food crop or a cash crop based on its use.
Explain whether the crop feeds people or is sold for industrial use.
Connect cash crops to the industries they supply, such as cotton to textiles.

worked_examples.question: Is sugarcane a food crop or a cash crop? Justify.
worked_examples.solution: Sugarcane is grown mainly for sale and supplies sugar mills, so it is a cash crop.

worked_examples.question: Classify rice and cotton as food or cash crops.
worked_examples.solution: Rice is a food crop grown for consumption; cotton is a cash crop grown for the textile industry.
worked_examples.answer: Rice = food crop; cotton = cash crop

exercises.question: Differentiate between food crops and cash crops with two examples each.
Name a cash crop and the industry it supports.
Explain the economic importance of cash crops in Indian agriculture.

concepts.title: Agricultural Development and Green Revolution
concepts.definition: Agricultural development means increasing farm output through modern inputs and technology. The Green Revolution introduced High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers, and irrigation to boost food grain production.
concepts.key_idea: The Green Revolution of the 1960s sharply increased wheat and rice production in India through HYV seeds and modern inputs, mainly in Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh.
question_patterns: What is meant by agricultural development?
Explain the main features of the Green Revolution.
Which crops benefited most from the Green Revolution and why?
Name the states where the Green Revolution had the greatest impact.
What inputs made the Green Revolution possible?

solution_steps.explain: Explain increasing production through modern inputs and technology.
Identify HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, pesticides, and irrigation.
Describe the rise in wheat and rice output and the leading states.

worked_examples.question: Which two crops were most affected by the Green Revolution?
worked_examples.solution: The Green Revolution mainly boosted wheat and rice production using HYV seeds.

worked_examples.question: Name two states where the Green Revolution was most successful.
worked_examples.solution: Punjab and Haryana adopted HYV seeds and irrigation most widely.

exercises.question: What is the Green Revolution? List its main features.
Why did the Green Revolution succeed mainly in northern India?
Discuss the positive and negative impacts of the Green Revolution.

concepts.title: Impact of Globalisation on Agriculture
concepts.definition: Globalisation has opened Indian agriculture to world markets, bringing new technology and export opportunities but also exposing farmers to competition from subsidised imports.
concepts.key_idea: Globalisation offers better prices and modern inputs for some crops, but small farmers face challenges due to reduced subsidies and competition with cheap imports.
question_patterns: How has globalisation affected Indian agriculture?
What are the benefits of globalisation for farmers?
What challenges do small farmers face due to globalisation?
Name two crops that benefit from export opportunities.
Explain the role of MSP in the context of globalisation.

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the impact is positive (exports, technology) or negative (competition, lower subsidies).
Describe how world prices, imports, or technology reach Indian farmers.
Summarise the benefit or challenge for the farmer.

worked_examples.question: How has globalisation helped farmers growing cotton?
worked_examples.solution: Cotton farmers can access export markets and modern technology, getting better prices.
worked_examples.answer: Access to export markets and better prices

worked_examples.question: What is a major challenge of globalisation for small farmers?
worked_examples.solution: Small farmers face competition from cheap, subsidised imports and reduced domestic support.

exercises.question: Explain two positive effects of globalisation on Indian agriculture.
Why do small farmers find it difficult to compete in a globalised market?
Discuss the impact of globalisation on Indian agriculture with examples.

concepts.title: Contribution of Agriculture to the Economy
concepts.definition: Agriculture is the backbone of the Indian economy, providing livelihood to about two-thirds of the population, supplying raw materials to industries, and contributing to exports.
concepts.key_idea: Agriculture supports food security, employment, industrial raw material, and export earnings; its share in GDP has declined but it remains the largest employer.
question_patterns: How does agriculture contribute to the Indian economy?
What share of the population depends on agriculture for livelihood?
Name two industries that depend on agricultural raw materials.
Why is agriculture called the backbone of the economy?
Explain the role of agriculture in providing employment.

solution_steps.explain: Note employment, food supply, raw materials, and exports.
Connect farm output to agro-based industries such as textiles and sugar.
State agriculture's overall importance to the economy.

worked_examples.question: Name two industries that depend on agricultural raw materials.
worked_examples.solution: The cotton textile industry and the sugar industry depend on agricultural raw materials.

worked_examples.question: Approximately what fraction of India's population depends on agriculture for a livelihood?
worked_examples.solution: About two-thirds of the working population depends on agriculture.

exercises.question: Explain how agriculture supports industries in India.
Why is agriculture still the largest employer despite its declining GDP share?
Discuss the contribution of agriculture to the Indian economy.

concepts.title: Sustainable Agriculture
concepts.definition: Sustainable agriculture is farming that meets current food needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs, using practices that conserve soil, water, and biodiversity.
concepts.key_idea: Organic farming, crop rotation, mixed farming, and reduced chemical use protect natural resources and ensure long-term productivity.
question_patterns: What is sustainable agriculture?
Name two practices that promote sustainable agriculture.
How does organic farming help sustainability?
Why is crop rotation considered a sustainable practice?
Explain the need for sustainable agriculture in India.

solution_steps.explain: Explain meeting present needs without harming future productivity.
Identify practices such as organic farming, crop rotation, and mixed farming.
Describe how the practice conserves soil, water, and biodiversity.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of a sustainable farming practice.
worked_examples.solution: Crop rotation alternates crops to maintain soil fertility and reduce pests.

worked_examples.question: Why is reducing chemical fertiliser use part of sustainable agriculture?
worked_examples.solution: Fewer chemicals preserve soil health and prevent water pollution.
worked_examples.answer: It preserves soil health and prevents water pollution

exercises.question: Define sustainable agriculture and give two examples of related practices.
How does organic farming contribute to sustainable agriculture?
Explain the importance of sustainable agriculture for future food security.
